title: Applyr v1: automated Glints/JobStreet job-application assistant
description:
## Problem Statement

Job hunting on Glints and JobStreet is repetitive and slow. The user has to re-run the same searches every day, spot which postings are new, and write a CV and cover letter for each role worth applying to. Tailoring by hand takes too long to do for every posting. Generic documents get worse results. Generating documents with an AI naively is risky, because the model might invent job titles, employers, dates, or achievements the user never had. Nothing today ties these steps together or tracks where each posting stands.

## Solution

Applyr is a single-user, self-hosted Laravel app that runs the whole loop automatically:

1. The user saves one or more **SearchProfiles**. On a schedule, each platform's **Adapter** (Glints, JobStreet) calls that platform's internal GraphQL job-search API and turns the results into canonical **Jobs**.
2. Each Job is new only if its `(platform, external_id)` pair has not been seen before. A new Job gets exactly one **Application** in `pending_tailoring`. A Job seen before is refreshed in place and never tailored again.
3. For each new Application, the app asks Gemini (Flash, free tier) to reframe only the free-text parts of the user's **MasterProfile** (descriptions, achievements, summary) and to write the cover-letter paragraphs. The response is structured JSON. The app checks the response against the facts in code; if the check fails, the attempt is thrown away and generated again.
4. A result that passes becomes a **TailoredApplication**. It is a self-contained JSON snapshot rendered through Blade into two PDFs (`cv.pdf`, `cover_letter.pdf`) with Browsershot. The Application moves to `needs_review` and the user gets a Telegram message.
5. On the dashboard (no auth) the user reviews and edits the documents, regenerates, rejects, or marks the Application applied after submitting it on the platform themselves. Every action can be undone.
6. If an Adapter keeps failing (Cloudflare challenge, API error, response shape drift, or network failure), it pauses itself, sends one Telegram alert, and waits for the user to press Resume on the dashboard.

## User Stories

### SearchProfiles

1. As the user, I want to create a named SearchProfile, so that I can save a search I care about and recognize it later.
2. As the user, I want to enter several keywords on a SearchProfile, so that postings matching any of them are found (OR-matched).
3. As the user, I want to set a free-text location (e.g. "Jakarta Selatan") and a country code, so that searches are scoped geographically.
4. As the user, I want to set optional minimum and maximum years of experience, so that I only see roles at my level.
5. As the user, I want to choose a post-date range (past 24 hours, past week, past month, any time), so that I only see recent postings.
6. As the user, I want to filter by work arrangement (remote, onsite, hybrid, any), so that I only see arrangements I would accept.
7. As the user, I want to filter by job type (full-time, part-time, contract, internship, any), so that I only see the kinds of employment I want.
8. As the user, I want several SearchProfiles active at once, so that I can track different kinds of roles in parallel.
9. As the user, I want to pause and resume a SearchProfile without deleting it, so that I can stop a search temporarily and keep its history.
10. As the user, I want to edit and delete SearchProfiles, so that my searches stay current.
11. As the user, I want each SearchProfile applied to both Glints and JobStreet, with each Adapter translating as much as its platform supports, so that I don't maintain separate searches per platform.
12. As the user, I want a filter a platform can't express to be approximated or ignored instead of making the search fail, so that one unsupported field doesn't stop results from that platform.

### Finding Jobs

13. As the user, I want every active SearchProfile polled automatically on a schedule, so that new postings are found without my involvement.
14. As the user, I want Glints postings fetched through Glints' internal GraphQL job-search API, so that results are structured and reliable rather than scraped from HTML.
15. As the user, I want JobStreet postings fetched through JobStreet's internal GraphQL job-search API on id.jobstreet.com, so that results are structured and reliable rather than scraped from HTML.
16. As the user, I want Adapters to send realistic browser headers and pace their requests, so that Cloudflare doesn't block them.
17. As the user, I want Jobs from both platforms normalized into one shape (title, company, location, country, URL, description, work arrangement, job type, experience bounds, salary, posted date, status), so that the dashboard shows every Job the same way.
18. As the user, I want the full raw platform response kept with each Job, so that platform-specific details (skills, benefits, categories) can be used later without fetching again.
19. As the user, I want a posting I've already seen to never create a second Application, so that I'm not asked to review or tailor the same Job twice.
20. As the user, I want a Job that several of my SearchProfiles match to still produce exactly one Application, so that overlapping searches don't create duplicates.
21. As the user, I want to see which SearchProfiles matched a Job and when, so that I understand why it appeared.
22. As the user, I want Jobs refreshed on later polls so that status changes (open, closed, expired) show up, so that I don't waste time on postings that have closed.
23. As the user, I want a JobStreet Job's status left as "unknown" when it can't be worked out, rather than assumed to be open, so that the status shown is never a guess.
24. As the user, I want salary kept as each platform reports it (min, max, currency, period) without converting between monthly and yearly, so that the numbers are never distorted.
25. As the user, I want a Job refresh to never change documents already generated for it, so that my reviewed CV and cover letter stay exactly as they were.

### MasterProfile

26. As the user, I want to fill in my MasterProfile on one scrollable dashboard page (personal info, skills, experience, education, projects), so that all my source-of-truth data is in one place.
27. As the user, I want the MasterProfile available without a separate "create profile" step, so that I can just start filling it in.
28. As the user, I want to enter my name, email, phone, location, and professional summary, so that my CV header and cover letter letterhead are correct.
29. As the user, I want to add any number of labelled links (LinkedIn, GitHub, portfolio, etc.), so that I'm not limited to a fixed set of link types.
30. As the user, I want to upload an optional profile photo and choose separately whether it appears on CVs, so that uploading a photo doesn't force it onto every CV.
31. As the user, I want to organize my skills into categories I name myself, so that the CV lists them grouped the way I think about them.
32. As the user, I want to add, edit, and delete experience entries (title, company, location, start/end month and year, "current" flag, employment type, description, achievements, skills used), so that my work history is complete.
33. As the user, I want to add, edit, and delete education entries (institution, degree, field of study, dates, "current" flag, description), so that my education is complete.
34. As the user, I want to add, edit, and delete projects (name, optional dates, "current" flag, tech stack, link, description, achievements), so that I can show work outside my employment history.
35. As the user, I want ticking "current" to clear and disable the end date, so that "still ongoing" is never confused with "not filled in".
36. As the user, I want the form to block saving when an end date is before its start date, or missing while "current" is unticked, so that bad dates never reach a CV.
37. As the user, I want every list shown newest first by start date, so that the order matches CV convention without manual reordering.

### AI tailoring

38. As the user, I want tailoring to start automatically for each new Application, so that documents are waiting for me when I review.
39. As the user, I want the AI to rewrite only my professional summary and each entry's description and achievements, so that titles, companies, and dates always stay exactly as in my MasterProfile.
40. As the user, I want the AI to be allowed to keep fewer achievements per entry, but never more than I listed, so that the CV can be sharper without inventing accomplishments.
41. As the user, I want skills copied into the CV without passing through the AI, so that they can't be altered.
42. As the user, I want the AI to write only the cover letter's opening, body, and closing paragraphs, while the date, subject line, greeting, and sign-off are filled in by the app from Job and MasterProfile facts, so that the parts carrying facts are always correct.
43. As the user, I want the AI's output to be structured JSON enforced by a response schema, so that it never has to be parsed out of free text.
44. As the user, I want each AI output entry tied to its MasterProfile entry by ID rather than by position, so that a skipped or reordered entry can't attach the wrong text to the wrong job.
45. As the user, I want every AI output checked in code before anything is rendered, so that invalid content never becomes a document.
46. As the user, I want a failed attempt thrown away and a fresh one generated, up to a retry limit, so that only a valid result is kept.
47. As the user, I want the Application marked `tailoring_failed` when all retries fail, so that I can see it and retry manually.
48. As the user, I want Gemini calls throttled to the free-tier limit (about 8 per minute) through a queue rate limiter, so that a burst of new Jobs doesn't exhaust my quota.
49. As the user, I want an HTTP 429 from Gemini retried with exponential backoff and not counted as a failed validation attempt, so that rate limits don't use up my regeneration attempts.
50. As the user, I want the AI provider hidden behind one interface, so that I can switch providers later without touching the pipeline.

### Rendering documents

51. As the user, I want every TailoredApplication rendered as two separate PDFs (CV and cover letter), so that I can upload them separately where platforms ask for them separately.
52. As the user, I want a minimalist, single-column, black-text CV in Inter with a thin rule under each section heading, so that ATS parsers read it easily and it looks professional.
53. As the user, I want CV sections in the order Header, Professional Summary, Skills, Experience, Education, Projects, with any empty section left out entirely, so that the CV never shows empty headings.
54. As the user, I want dates shown as "Jan 2022 – Mar 2024", or "Present" for current entries, so that dates look consistent.
55. As the user, I want my photo shown top-left in the CV header (100×100, rounded square) only when "show photo" is on, and never on the cover letter, so that I control where my photo appears.
56. As the user, I want skills shown one line per category, so that the Skills section stays compact.
57. As the user, I want the cover letter laid out as letterhead, date, "Re: Application for {job title}", "Dear {company} Hiring Team", paragraphs, "Sincerely, {full name}", so that it follows standard letter format.
58. As the user, I want the font bundled with the app instead of loaded from a CDN, so that PDF rendering never fails for lack of network access.
59. As the user, I want documents rendered entirely from the TailoredApplication's stored snapshot, so that editing my MasterProfile later never silently changes documents already generated.

### Reviewing and tracking Applications

60. As the user, I want a Telegram message when an Application reaches `needs_review`, so that I know there's something to review.
61. As the user, I want a dashboard list of Applications filterable by status, so that I can see what needs my attention.
62. As the user, I want an Application's detail page to show the Job's details, which SearchProfiles matched it, and previews of both PDFs, so that I can judge the documents in context.
63. As the user, I want a link from the Application to the posting's URL, so that I can go and apply on the platform.
64. As the user, I want to edit the summary, descriptions, achievements, and cover-letter paragraphs in place while the Application is in `needs_review`, then have the PDFs rendered again, so that I can polish documents before applying.
65. As the user, I want facts (title, company, dates, skills, contact details) not editable in that editor, so that my edits can't break the fact rule either.
66. As the user, I want edited Applications flagged as edited by me, so that I can tell AI-only documents from ones I touched.
67. As the user, I want to regenerate an Application's documents, with the current documents still visible until the new ones replace them, so that I never lose a usable version while waiting.
68. As the user, I want to mark an Application as applied after submitting it myself, with the time recorded, so that I know what I've applied to and when.
69. As the user, I want to reject an Application at any stage (pending, failed, or in review), with the time recorded, so that I can drop Jobs I don't want.
70. As the user, I want to retry tailoring on a `tailoring_failed` Application, so that a temporary failure isn't a dead end.
71. As the user, I want to undo "applied" (back to `needs_review`) and undo "rejected" (back to exactly the status it had before), so that a misclick is easy to fix.
72. As the user, I want only the actions valid for the current status offered, as named buttons (Reject / Retry / Regenerate / Mark Applied / Undo), so that I can never reach a meaningless state.
73. As the user, I want to download an Application's CV and cover letter PDFs from the dashboard, so that I can upload them to the platform.

### Adapter health

74. As the user, I want each Adapter's failures classified as anti-bot block, transport failure, structured API error, or response-shape drift, so that alerts tell me what actually went wrong.
75. As the user, I want an HTTP 403 with a `Cf-Mitigated: challenge` header recognized as an anti-bot block, so that Cloudflare blocking is identified precisely.
76. As the user, I want a 200 response that no longer maps onto the expected Job fields treated as response-shape drift, so that silent API changes are caught.
77. As the user, I want Glints and JobStreet health tracked independently, so that one broken platform doesn't affect the other.
78. As the user, I want an Adapter to alert only after 3 consecutive broken failures (anti-bot, API error, or shape drift, mixed categories counting together), so that a one-off glitch doesn't page me.
79. As the user, I want transport failures to get a longer leash (6 consecutive failures) before alerting, so that brief network trouble doesn't page me.
80. As the user, I want any successful run to reset an Adapter's failure count, so that alerts reflect streaks of failures that are still happening.
81. As the user, I want exactly one Telegram alert when a threshold is crossed, naming the platform, failure category, count against threshold, first and last failure times, status code and a short error snippet, and a note that the Adapter is paused, so that I have everything I need to diagnose it.
82. As the user, I want an Adapter paused automatically once it alerts, with no repeat reminders, so that the app stops hitting a platform that is blocking it and doesn't spam me.
83. As the user, I want an Adapters page showing each Adapter's status (Healthy / Failing n of threshold / Paused), last successful run, last failure details, and a short history of recent failures, so that I can see pipeline health at a glance.
84. As the user, I want a Resume button on a paused Adapter that resets its counters and puts it back on the normal schedule, so that I decide when it runs again.

### Operating the app

85. As the user, I want the dashboard to need no login, so that my personal tool has no friction.
86. As the user, I want the Telegram bot token, chat ID, Gemini API key, Gemini model, poll schedule, and retry limits set in environment config, so that I can operate the app without code changes.

## Implementation Decisions

### Stack and shape

- New Laravel app scaffolded at the repo root: queue workers, the scheduler, Blade views, and Browsershot for PDFs. There is one user and no authentication.
- The domain vocabulary is exactly as in CONTEXT.md: SearchProfile, Adapter, Job, MasterProfile, TailoredApplication, Application. Code names follow it.
- The dashboard is server-rendered Blade. Whether to add an interactivity layer (Livewire, Alpine, etc.) is the implementer's choice, as long as every behavior below can be tested through HTTP routes.

### Schema (from the closed designs in applyr-n58.2, .3, .4, .5, .6, .7)

- **search_profiles**: name (required), is_active, keyword (string array), location (free text), country_code (unconstrained string; only "ID" is actually supported), min_experience_years and max_experience_years (nullable ints), post_date_range enum {PAST_24_HOURS, PAST_WEEK, PAST_MONTH, ANY_TIME}, work_arrangement enum {remote, onsite, hybrid, any}, job_type enum {full_time, part_time, contract, internship, any}. It holds no run or poll state. Salary floor is not part of v1.
- **jobs**: platform enum {glints, jobstreet}, external_id, title, company_name, location, country_code, url, description, work_arrangement enum {remote, onsite, hybrid, unspecified}, job_type enum {full_time, part_time, contract, internship, unspecified}, min_years_experience and max_years_experience (nullable), status enum {open, closed, expired, unknown}, salary_min and salary_max (nullable numeric), salary_currency (nullable ISO), salary_period enum {monthly, yearly, unspecified} (nullable), posted_date (timestamp), raw_payload (the full raw JSON). A composite unique index on (platform, external_id) is the dedup check. There is no Company entity.
- **job_search_profile_matches** pivot: job_id, search_profile_id, matched_at. One row per (Job, SearchProfile) pair, recorded the first time that pair is seen. Informational only.
- **master_profile**: a single mutable row with no user_id and no versioning. Fields: full_name, email (both required), phone, location, professional_summary, links (JSON array of {label, url}), skills (JSON array of {category, skills[]}), photo_path (nullable), show_photo (bool).
  - **experiences** (children, sorted by start_date desc): title, company, location, start_date, end_date, is_current, employment_type, description, achievements (string array), skills_used.
  - **educations** (children, sorted by start_date desc): institution, degree, field_of_study, start_date, end_date, is_current, description.
  - **projects** (children, sorted by start_date desc): name, start_date, end_date, is_current, tech_stack, link, description, achievements.
  - Dates are month and year only; the day is stored as the 1st. The child row's primary key is the `entry_id` used throughout tailoring.
- **applications**: job_id (unique), status enum {pending_tailoring, tailoring_failed, needs_review, applied, rejected}, current_tailored_application_id (nullable FK), applied_at, rejected_at, previous_status, edited_by_user.
- **tailored_applications**: application_id, cv_data (JSON snapshot), cover_letter_data (JSON snapshot), cv_pdf_path, cover_letter_pdf_path, timestamps. Superseded rows may stay in the database; only the row the Application points to is shown.
- **Adapter health state**, one row per platform:
  - status: healthy, failing, or paused
  - broken-track and transport-track consecutive counters
  - first_failure_at and last_failure_at for the current streak
  - last_success_at
  - last failure category, status code, and error snippet
  - a bounded recent-failure log (category + timestamp)

### Modules

- **Adapter (one per platform)** is a deep module behind one shared interface. Input: a SearchProfile. Output: canonical Job data (not yet persisted) plus the raw payload per posting.
  - Internally it translates the SearchProfile into the platform's native search input as best it can, sends the GraphQL requests with realistic browser headers, pages through results up to a configurable page cap, paces requests, and maps each result to canonical fields.
  - It reports failures only as four typed exceptions: anti-bot blocked, transport, API error, shape drift. Shape drift is thrown when a required canonical field can't be mapped from a 200 response that has no GraphQL errors.
  - **Glints Adapter**: POST glints.com/api/v2/graphql, `searchJobsV3(data: JobSearchConditionInput)`. It maps keyword→SearchTerm, country→CountryCode, post_date_range→lastUpdatedAtRange, experience→min/maxYearsOfExperience, work arrangement→isRemote/workArrangementOptions. Location is resolved to Glints location/city IDs as best it can.
    - On the Job side: posted_date←createdAt (not startDate or expiryDate), url←externalApplyURL, description←descriptionJsonString flattened to text, status mapped directly from Glints' status.
  - **JobStreet Adapter**: POST id.jobstreet.com/graphql (never jobstreet.co.id), `jobSearchV7(params: JobSearchV7QueryInput!)` with a client-generated sessionId and searchContext brand/intent/source.
    - The request needs the full realistic header set (Accept, Accept-Language, sec-ch-ua*, UA).
    - On the Job side: posted_date←listedAt, url←url, description←abstract, country_code taken from the request context, status derived from expiry when available, otherwise `unknown`, min/max years of experience are null.
    - **Build step, not a blocker:** where keyword, location, date range, and pagination go inside JobSearchV7QueryInput is still unknown. Capture one real outgoing request from browser devtools, save it as a fixture, and implement the mapping against it.
- **Poll orchestration.** A scheduled command queues one run per Adapter that isn't paused. The run covers every active SearchProfile. For each Job returned:
  - Upsert by (platform, external_id), refreshing the core fields and raw_payload.
  - Record the pivot row if this (Job, SearchProfile) pair is new.
  - Only if the Job was newly created: create its Application in `pending_tailoring` and queue tailoring.
  - Being returned by an Adapter for a SearchProfile counts as "matched". There is no second, app-side filter in v1.
- **Adapter health handler.** A shared queue-layer handler that doesn't know about platforms. It wraps each Adapter run, catches the four typed exceptions, and updates health state.
  - Broken track (anti-bot, API error, shape drift): pause at 3 consecutive failures.
  - Transport track: within a run it retries with backoff; the run counts once. It escalates at 6 consecutive failed runs.
  - A run that finishes cleanly resets both counters. A failure on one track does not reset the other track's counter.
  - Crossing a threshold sets status to paused and sends one Telegram alert. A paused Adapter is skipped by the scheduler.
  - The dashboard Resume action resets the counters and sets status to healthy. It does not trigger an immediate run.
- **AI provider interface.** A single interface: given a prompt and a JSON response schema, return decoded structured data. It throws a typed rate-limited error (for 429) or a typed provider error. The Gemini implementation calls generateContent with `responseSchema` over Laravel's HTTP client; model ID and API key come from config. The pipeline depends only on the interface.
- **Tailoring pipeline**, a queued job per Application.
  - **Before starting:** it re-checks that the Application is still `pending_tailoring` and exits quietly if not. This covers a user rejecting it mid-flight.
  - **Prompt:** built from the Job (title, company, description) and the MasterProfile. Each Experience, Education, and Project entry is sent with its entry_id, its facts as read-only context, and its reframeable text.
  - **Response schema:** kept narrow, only what the AI writes:
    ```
    { professional_summary: string,
      entries: [{ entry_id, description, achievements: string[] }],
      cover_letter: { opening_paragraph, body_paragraphs: string[], closing_paragraph } }
    ```
  - **Fact validation:** runs in code before any render. It fails if:
    - an entry_id is unknown or duplicated
    - an entry has more achievements than MasterProfile's list for that entry
    - the summary or a cover-letter paragraph is required but empty
    - the output fails the schema

    An entry the AI leaves out falls back to its original MasterProfile text word for word.
  - **Regeneration:** a failed validation throws the attempt away and generates again, up to a configurable limit (default 3). When the limit is exhausted, status becomes `tailoring_failed`.
  - **Rate limiting:** Gemini calls go through a queue rate limiter (about 8 per minute, configurable). A 429 releases the job with exponential backoff and does not use up a validation attempt. The two retry paths stay separate.
  - **Snapshot assembly:** on success the app builds cv_data and cover_letter_data.
    - cv_data holds personal_info (facts + reframed summary + photo_path/show_photo), skills copied word for word, and experience/education/projects entries keyed by entry_id with copied facts + reframed text.
    - cover_letter_data holds the app-assembled greeting "Dear {company_name} Hiring Team", date, subject "Re: Application for {job.title}", and sign-off "Sincerely, {full_name}", plus the three AI-written paragraph fields.
  - **Finish:** it renders both PDFs, creates the TailoredApplication, repoints current_tailored_application_id, sets status to `needs_review`, and sends the Telegram review notification.
- **Document renderer** has two parts.
  - Two Blade views (CV and cover letter) that take a snapshot and nothing else. They follow the layout rules in the user stories (section order, omit-if-empty, date format, photo rules, bundled Inter .woff2 fonts).
  - A **PdfRenderer interface** (HTML in → PDF file path out), with a Browsershot implementation. This is the only new test seam besides the app boundary.
- **Application state machine.** A single place that owns the transition table from applyr-n58.4 and rejects any other transition:
  - create → pending_tailoring
  - pending_tailoring → needs_review / tailoring_failed / rejected
  - tailoring_failed → pending_tailoring (retry) / rejected
  - needs_review → pending_tailoring (regenerate) / applied / rejected
  - applied → needs_review (undo)
  - rejected → previous_status (undo)
  - previous_status is set on entering applied or rejected; the applied_at and rejected_at timestamps are set and cleared as the table specifies.
  - Retry, regenerate, and an undo that lands in `pending_tailoring` all queue tailoring. On regenerate the old TailoredApplication stays current until it's replaced.
- **Tailored content editing.** Only while in `needs_review`. The editor exposes only the reframeable fields in the snapshot: summary, per-entry description and achievements, and cover-letter paragraphs. Saving writes the snapshot, sets edited_by_user, renders both PDFs again, and leaves status unchanged.
- **Telegram notifier.** Sends Bot API sendMessage over Laravel's HTTP client to one configured chat. It sends two message types: the review notification (Job title, company, platform, dashboard link) and the Adapter pause alert (content as in story 81). No Telegram-driven actions.
- **Dashboard routes/pages**: Applications list and detail (with actions, editor, PDF preview/download), SearchProfiles CRUD, MasterProfile single-page form (per-row CRUD and photo upload, with date validation), Adapters health page with Resume.

## Testing Decisions

- **Good tests** exercise behavior the user can observe through the app's outer boundary and assert outcomes: database rows and statuses, HTTP responses from dashboard routes, outbound HTTP requests sent (their payloads), and renderer input. They never assert internal calls, private methods, or class structure, so internals can be refactored freely.
- **Seam 1: the app boundary.** Tests drive the app only as production does: the scheduled poll command, queued jobs (sync queue in tests, so a poll runs the whole pipeline end to end), and dashboard HTTP routes.
  - All outbound I/O is faked with Laravel's HTTP client fake, and stray requests are blocked: Glints GraphQL, JobStreet GraphQL, Gemini generateContent, and Telegram sendMessage. This requires every external call to go through Laravel's HTTP client.
  - Adapter fixtures are real response bodies saved as JSON. For JobStreet this includes the captured browser request. Drift and block cases are made by editing those fixtures (a field renamed, `errors` array present, 403 with `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`, connection exception).
  - Gemini is faked with response sequences to cover: valid first attempt, invalid-then-valid, invalid until exhausted, and 429-then-valid (checking that a 429 doesn't use up a validation attempt).
  - Rate limiting and backoff are tested by moving time forward, not by sleeping.
- **Seam 2: PdfRenderer.** In tests a fake PdfRenderer records the HTML it receives and writes a placeholder file. Template behavior is asserted on that HTML: section order, empty sections left out, date formatting, photo shown only when enabled and only on the CV, cover-letter greeting/subject/sign-off. One smoke test runs the real Browsershot implementation and is skipped when Chromium isn't available.
- **What gets tested (all through the two seams):**
  - Polling: normalization per platform, dedup and upsert, pivot rows, one Application per Job across overlapping SearchProfiles, no re-tailoring on re-poll, status refresh.
  - Adapter health: each failure category, both thresholds, mixed-category counting, reset on success, a single alert, pause skipping scheduled runs, Resume.
  - Tailoring: fact validation rules, regeneration and exhaustion, the separate 429 path, snapshot contents, fallback for omitted entries, Telegram review message, and the in-flight-reject guard.
  - Application actions: every allowed transition through dashboard routes, every disallowed transition rejected, undo restoring the exact previous status, regenerate keeping the old TailoredApplication until replaced.
  - Editing: only reframeable fields change, PDFs rendered again, status unchanged, edited flag set.
  - MasterProfile form: validation, the current/end-date rule, photo upload and toggle, sort order. SearchProfile CRUD and pause.
- **Prior art:** none yet; the repo has no code. Follow Laravel's documented feature-testing patterns (HTTP client fake with stray-request prevention, database refresh per test, time travel). The request/response facts recorded in applyr-n58.1 are the reference for fixtures.

## Out of Scope

- A LinkedIn Adapter, or any platform other than Glints and JobStreet.
- Multi-user support, authentication, or tenancy.
- CV or cover-letter template variants per role; v1 has exactly one generic template for each.
- Submitting applications automatically, or polling a platform for real-world outcomes (employer rejection, interview, offer).
- A status-change history log, and reject reasons or notes.
- Detecting a broken Adapter from zero results (a clean 200 with no Jobs).
- Resuming an Adapter or taking any other action through Telegram.
- A salary-floor filter, salary normalization between monthly and yearly, or a normalized Company entity.
- Versioning the MasterProfile, per-entry visibility toggles, manual ordering of entries, or a profile-completeness check before generation.
- Supporting countries other than Indonesia.
- Deployment and hosting.

## Further Notes

- **Source:** the closed Wayfinder map applyr-n58 and its children n58.1–n58.7 hold the full grilled rationale. CONTEXT.md holds the locked vocabulary. There are no ADRs yet.
- **Choices made while writing this spec, not settled by the map.** Revisit any that feel wrong:
  - **Counting a run:** one scheduled run of an Adapter across all active SearchProfiles counts as one attempt for health purposes.
  - **Separate counters:** the two health tracks keep separate counters, and a failure on one doesn't reset the other.
  - **Match rule:** "matched" means the Adapter returned the Job for that SearchProfile, with no app-side filter afterwards.
  - **Omitted entries:** an entry the AI leaves out falls back to its original text.
  - **Retry default:** the regeneration limit defaults to 3.
  - **Undo re-queues:** an undo that lands in `pending_tailoring` queues tailoring again.
  - **Job refreshes:** the "never overwrite consumed fields" rule is met by the TailoredApplication snapshot. Job core columns refresh freely, and documents never read live Job data.
- **Known gap:** applyr-n58.4 says `tailoring_failed` should "fold into n58.7's consecutive-failure alerting", but n58.7 only covers Adapters. In v1, `tailoring_failed` shows up only on the dashboard and sends no Telegram message. A tailoring-health alert (for example, a revoked Gemini key failing every Application) would be follow-up work.
- **Poll schedule:** not fixed by the map. Make it configurable, with a conservative default (e.g. hourly), to limit Cloudflare scoring risk.
- **Rate-limit evidence:** n58.1 saw no rate limiting in bursts of 10–15 requests. That doesn't rule out throttling at higher volume, so keep pacing and backoff.

title: Design adapter monitoring/alerting strategy
description:
## Question

How does the system detect and alert on an Adapter breaking (HTML selector changed, internal JSON API shape changed, or anti-bot blocking kicked in), given confirmed decisions: alerts reuse the Telegram bot channel, and alerting fires after consecutive failures rather than on the first failure?

This ticket is blocked on the platform-API prototype ticket: the real failure modes (structured JSON error vs. HTML parse exception vs. CAPTCHA/block page vs. timeout) determine what "failure" even means to detect, which can't be designed from guesswork. Once unblocked, grill: what counts as a distinguishable failure per platform, the consecutive-failure threshold, what the Telegram alert message contains, whether a broken Adapter auto-pauses (stops attempting further runs until acknowledged) or keeps retrying on schedule, and how this is surfaced on the dashboard (not just Telegram).
notes:
## Decision

### Failure taxonomy (per Adapter, Glints/JobStreet counted independently)
1. **Anti-bot block** — HTTP 403 with `Cf-Mitigated: challenge` header (or any Cloudflare interstitial instead of JSON). Matches the concrete signature n58.1 observed on both platforms.
2. **Transport failure** — timeout, DNS failure, connection refused/reset (no response at all).
3. **Structured API error** — a response came back but is a non-2xx status (not matching #1), or a 200 whose GraphQL body contains an `errors` array.
4. **Response-shape drift** — HTTP 200, no GraphQL errors, but the body fails to map onto the Adapter's expected Job fields (missing/renamed/retyped field) — the JSON-API equivalent of "selector changed". HTML-parse-exception was dropped from the taxonomy since neither Adapter parses HTML (n58.1: both platforms are pure JSON GraphQL APIs, no Browsershot/selector fallback needed).

Detection lives inside each Adapter (it already owns response parsing and knows its expected shape) via typed exceptions (e.g. `AntiBotBlockedException`, `TransportException`, `ApiErrorException`, `ShapeDriftException`); a shared, platform-agnostic queue-layer handler catches these uniformly to do counting/threshold/alert/pause.

Zero-results-but-clean-response (200, valid shape, no errors, but 0 jobs across consecutive runs) is explicitly OUT of scope for this ticket — indistinguishable from a legitimately quiet SearchProfile without a separate baselining design.

### Two-track consecutive-failure counting
- **Broken track**: anti-bot block + structured API error + shape drift share ONE counter per Adapter — mixed categories count together. Threshold: **3 consecutive failures**.
- **Transient track**: transport failures get backoff-retry and a longer leash. Threshold: **6 consecutive failures**, after which they escalate into the same alert/pause path as the broken track.
- Any successful run resets the counter to 0. "Consecutive" means consecutive run attempts, not calendar time (polling cadence isn't fixed yet).

### Alert + pause behavior
- Crossing either threshold fires exactly ONE Telegram alert (not one per subsequent failure) and auto-pauses the Adapter — no further scheduled runs until acknowledged. This avoids alert spam and avoids hammering a platform that may be rate-limiting/IP-scoring the requests.
- No repeat/nagging reminders while paused — single-user personal tool; one alert plus the persistent "Paused" dashboard state is enough.

### Telegram alert message content
Platform name (Glints/JobStreet), human-readable failure category, consecutive count vs. threshold (e.g. "3/3"), timestamp of first and most recent failure in the streak, a short technical detail line (status code + truncated error snippet), and a closing line stating the Adapter is paused and needs dashboard acknowledgement to resume.

### Resume mechanism
Dashboard-only "Resume" button (NOT via Telegram reply — keeps one interactive surface, consistent with how Application review/edit already happens on the dashboard). Resume = reset counter to 0 + re-enter normal schedule. No special immediate-retry path; if the next scheduled run fails again, it simply re-accumulates toward the same threshold and can re-alert.

### Dashboard surfacing
An Adapters view listing each Adapter (Glints, JobStreet) with: current status (Healthy / Failing n-of-threshold / Paused), last successful run timestamp, last failure's category + detail if any, a Resume button when Paused, and a short recent-failure history log (category + timestamp) per Adapter.
close_reason: Four-category failure taxonomy (anti-bot block, transport failure, structured API error, response-shape drift), detected in the Adapter via typed exceptions and counted by a shared queue-layer handler: two tracks (broken=3 consecutive, transient=6 consecutive escalating into the same path). Crossing threshold fires one Telegram alert and auto-pauses the Adapter; dashboard-only Resume button resets the counter. No repeat reminders. Dashboard shows per-Adapter health status, last failure, Resume action, and a short failure history. Zero-results soft-failure detection explicitly deferred. Full decision in issue notes.

title: Design CV/cover-letter HTML template
description:
## Question

What does the single generic Blade HTML template (rendered to PDF via Browsershot) for a TailoredApplication's CV and cover letter look like — layout, sections, and how it binds to TailoredApplication's structured JSON fields?

This ticket is blocked on both the MasterProfile schema ticket and the canonical Job model ticket: the template can't be designed until the fields it renders (experience entries, skills, education, projects from MasterProfile; job title/company/description context from Job) are locked. Per the map's Destination, this is ONE generic template for v1 — no per-role variants (SA vs QA out of scope). Grill: CV layout/sections, cover-letter structure, how the "reframed description/achievement" text from TailoredApplication slots in without touching the locked facts (title/company/period), and whether CV and cover letter are one PDF or two separate PDFs.
design:
## CV/cover-letter template design (v1)

### Output

Two separate PDFs per TailoredApplication — `cv.pdf` and `cover_letter.pdf` — each its own
Blade view, each its own Browsershot render call. Not a combined single-PDF document.

### Visual style

Minimalist, single-column, pure black text (no accent colors). Thin horizontal rule under
each section heading to separate sections. Font: Inter, self-hosted (Regular + Bold/Semibold
`.woff2` bundled with the template assets, `@font-face`'d in) — no Google Fonts CDN dependency,
so PDF rendering in the queue worker never depends on outbound network access at render time.
Natural page-length flow, no hard single-page cap (Browsershot/PDF paginate natively).

### CV sections (in order; a section is omitted entirely — no heading rendered — if its
underlying data is empty)

1. **Header** — name, email, phone, location, links (all facts). Optional profile photo:
   fixed 100x100px, rounded-square (not circular), positioned top-left beside the text block,
   shown only if `show_photo` is true. No role tagline under the name (MasterProfile has no
   "current title" concept; deriving one from the latest Experience entry was rejected as an
   undesired implicit fact-derivation rule).
2. **Professional Summary** — reframed text, single field (not array/ID-keyed — it's a
   MasterProfile singleton).
3. **Skills** — grouped by category, one line per category (e.g. "Programming Languages:
   JavaScript, Python, Go"). Copied verbatim from MasterProfile; skills never go through the
   Gemini call at all, since they're pure facts with nothing to reframe.
4. **Experience** — reverse-chronological. Per entry: facts (title, company, location,
   start/end date, employment_type) rendered as-is; description reframed; achievements
   reframed as a bulleted list that may shrink (AI can drop irrelevant bullets for a sharper
   CV) but never grow beyond MasterProfile's original count (inventing achievements would
   violate the "reframe only" rule).
5. **Education** — same fact/reframe split as Experience.
6. **Projects** — same fact/reframe split as Experience.

Date display format: `"Jan 2022 – Mar 2024"` (month abbreviation + 4-digit year, en dash),
`"Present"` when `is_current` is true.

### Cover letter structure

Letterhead (name/contact block, no photo) → date line → subject line
`"Re: Application for {job.title}"` → greeting `"Dear {company_name} Hiring Team"` (no
recruiter-name field exists anywhere in the data model, so this is the fixed default, not
AI-generated) → `opening_paragraph` → `body_paragraphs[]` → `closing_paragraph` → sign-off
`"Sincerely, {full_name}"`. No recipient address block (no address data exists for either
Job or a hiring contact). Only the three paragraph fields are AI-generated; greeting, date,
subject, and sign-off are deterministic, app-assembled from Job/MasterProfile facts.

### TailoredApplication JSON binding (self-contained snapshots — template renders entirely
from this JSON, no MasterProfile re-join at render time; this is the audit-trail mechanism
n58.3 already committed to)

**`cv_data`**:
- `personal_info`: full_name, email, phone, location, links, professional_summary
  (reframed), photo_path, show_photo — all copied/reframed at generation time
- `skills`: copied verbatim from MasterProfile (category groupings intact)
- `experience[]` / `education[]` / `projects[]`: each entry object keyed by its
  MasterProfile row's `entry_id`, carrying the copied facts (title/company/dates/etc.)
  plus the reframed description/achievements

**`cover_letter_data`**:
- Assembled facts: greeting, date, subject, sign_off
- AI-generated: opening_paragraph, body_paragraphs[], closing_paragraph

### Gemini `responseSchema` scope

Deliberately narrower than the full snapshot above — only what the AI actually writes:
- Per Experience/Education/Project entry: `{entry_id, description, achievements[]}`
- Cover letter: `{opening_paragraph, body_paragraphs[], closing_paragraph}`

The request includes each MasterProfile entry's `entry_id` so the response is ID-keyed
rather than positionally matched — robust to the AI skipping/reordering entries, and makes
programmatic fact-validation (the map's fixed pre-render check) a direct lookup: fetch the
MasterProfile row by `entry_id`, confirm the AI didn't touch title/company/period, since the
AI response never even carries those fields.

### MasterProfile schema amendment (reopens n58.3's closed design)

Adds two fields to MasterProfile (personal info) to support the optional photo:
- `photo_path` — nullable, dashboard-uploaded file
- `show_photo` — boolean, independent of whether a photo is uploaded, so uploading a photo
  doesn't force it onto every CV

## Decisions

- Two PDFs, not one — matches how job platforms/company portals request uploads separately
  (CV required, cover letter often distinct/optional), and keeps each layout independent.
- ATS-friendly minimalist style chosen deliberately over a more visually distinctive
  multi-column/sidebar layout, since documents flow through automated parsers on
  Glints/JobStreet and third-party ATS after that.
- Skills bypass the AI entirely (never sent to or received from Gemini) — they're pure facts
  per n58.3's fact/reframe split, so round-tripping them through the model would only add
  token cost and a risk surface for unwanted edits, with no upside.
- Achievements may shrink but never grow when reframed — a deliberate reading of "reframe
  only" (n58's fixed constraint): curating down to the most relevant bullets is reframing;
  fabricating new ones is not.
- Cover letter's greeting/date/subject/sign-off are template-assembled facts, not AI output —
  only the narrative paragraphs are actually generated, keeping the Gemini responseSchema
  minimal and validation trivial (nothing fact-bearing for the AI to get wrong there).
- TailoredApplication JSON is a full self-contained snapshot (facts + reframed content),
  keyed by MasterProfile entry_id, for both cv_data and cover_letter_data — consistent with
  n58.3's stated audit-trail rationale, and means template rendering never needs to re-join
  live MasterProfile state (which could have changed since generation).
- Font is Inter, self-hosted rather than CDN-loaded — Browsershot renders in a queue worker
  context where an outbound font fetch at render time is an unnecessary failure mode.
- Photo is optional via a dedicated `show_photo` toggle separate from `photo_path` — amends
  n58.3's MasterProfile schema (photo wasn't in scope there). Positioned top-left,
  100x100px rounded-square, only in the CV header (never on the cover letter letterhead).

Grilled and confirmed with user: 4 rounds, 18 questions.
close_reason: CV/cover-letter template grilled and confirmed with user (4 rounds, 18 questions). Two separate PDFs (cv.pdf/cover_letter.pdf), minimalist single-column Inter-font layout with section-separator rules, CV section list/order with omit-if-empty, ID-keyed fact+reframe JSON snapshot binding for TailoredApplication (cv_data/cover_letter_data), narrow Gemini responseSchema (skills bypass AI entirely; cover letter greeting/date/subject/sign-off are app-assembled facts, not AI output), achievements may shrink but not grow when reframed, optional photo toggle (amends MasterProfile from n58.3). Full design recorded in issue design field.

title: Design canonical Job model
description:
## Question

What is the canonical shape of a Job — the normalized model every Adapter (Glints, JobStreet) produces regardless of source? Which fields are "core" (present and harmonized across both platforms) vs "extra" (platform-specific, stored loosely)?

This ticket is blocked on the platform-API prototype ticket: the real field availability (e.g. salary range, remote/onsite tags, seniority level) from Glints and JobStreet needs to be known before the canonical model is locked, otherwise the schema is guesswork. Once unblocked, grill: field list and types, how platform+external_id (the dedup key) is stored, how posted_date is normalized across platforms with different date formats/granularity, and how a Job links to the SearchProfile match(es) that surfaced it.
design:
## Canonical Job model (v1)

### Job (core columns)

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| platform | enum: glints \| jobstreet | Part of the dedup key |
| external_id | string | Platform's raw job id; part of the dedup key |
| title | string | |
| company_name | string | No separate normalized Company entity in v1 |
| location | string (free text) | Same shape as SearchProfile.location |
| country_code | string | For JobStreet, populated from the Adapter/search request context (id.jobstreet.com is ID-scoped), not parsed from the job payload |
| url | string | The one link the dashboard sends the user to in order to apply/view — Glints' externalApplyURL, JobStreet's url; no separate detail-page field |
| description | text | Glints descriptionJsonString, JobStreet abstract — richness differs by platform, still one field |
| work_arrangement | enum: remote \| onsite \| hybrid \| unspecified | "unspecified" (not "any" — that's a SearchProfile filter wildcard, not a Job attribute) |
| job_type | enum: full_time \| part_time \| contract \| internship \| unspecified | Same enum family as SearchProfile.job_type minus "any" |
| min_years_experience | integer, nullable | Kept as core (nullable) even though JobStreet doesn't expose it, for dashboard-consistency with the SearchProfile filter |
| max_years_experience | integer, nullable | Same rationale |
| status | enum: open \| closed \| expired \| unknown | Glints: mapped directly from its status field. JobStreet: derived from expiry if available, else `unknown` — never guessed as `open`. Re-derived on every re-poll, not fixed at first ingest |
| salary_min | numeric, nullable | |
| salary_max | numeric, nullable | |
| salary_currency | string, nullable | ISO code |
| salary_period | enum: monthly \| yearly \| unspecified, nullable | Stored as each platform reports it — no monthly↔yearly normalization (lossy); pre-formatted display strings live in raw_payload instead |
| posted_date | timestamp | Glints -> createdAt (not startDate, which is likely employment start date, or expiryDate, which is application deadline). JobStreet -> listedAt. Always the best-available real timestamp; no bucket is stored on Job (buckets are a SearchProfile query-side concept only) |
| raw_payload | JSON | Full raw platform response, not a curated subset — cheaper to mine a new field later than to re-fetch |

### Dedup key

Composite unique index `(platform, external_id)`. No synthetic combined key column — the composite index is the dedup check, run before a Job enters AI tailoring (per the map's fixed architectural decision).

### Update semantics

Upsert on dedup match: re-fetching an already-seen `(platform, external_id)` refreshes core fields and `raw_payload` from the latest response (this is what makes `status` transitions like open->closed/expired observable over time). Fields already consumed by an Application/TailoredApplication are never retroactively overwritten by a later Job refresh.

### Job <-> SearchProfile linkage

Many-to-many pivot table `job_search_profile_matches` (`job_id`, `search_profile_id`, `matched_at`), one row per first-observed (Job, SearchProfile) pair. Purely informational for v1 (dashboard "why did this appear" display) — a second SearchProfile later matching an already-deduped Job adds a pivot row but does not re-trigger notification/tailoring, since exactly one Application exists per Job regardless of match count.

### Extra/platform-specific data

Not promoted to columns for v1: Glints skills/benefits/educationLevel/gender/labels, JobStreet categories/activity-analytics-counts/seoHierarchy, and both platforms' pre-formatted salary display strings. All available via `raw_payload` if/when actually needed.

## Decisions

- Core vs extra split: a field is core only if every Adapter can populate it the same way; min/max_years_experience is a deliberate exception (kept core+nullable for dashboard consistency with the SearchProfile filter it mirrors) despite JobStreet lacking it.
- skills (Glints) and tags (JobStreet) are NOT unified into one core field — different semantics (skill list vs generic tags) — both stay in raw_payload.
- No separate Company entity; company is a plain string column on Job for v1.
- Reference facts pulled from applyr-n58.1 findings (Glints searchJobsV3 Job fields; JobStreet jobSearchV7 Job fields) as the union basis for this schema.
close_reason: Canonical Job model grilled and confirmed with user (10 questions, 2 rounds). Core/extra field split, platform+external_id dedup key (composite unique index), posted_date normalized to a real timestamp per platform (no bucket stored), status enum re-derived on upsert, structured salary columns, and a Job-SearchProfile pivot table all recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md Job definition sharpened to match (composite dedup key, core-vs-raw_payload split, upsert-not-immutable, pivot linkage).

title: Design Application status-tracking flow
description:
## Question

What states does an Application move through on the dashboard, and what are the valid transitions between them? Per CONTEXT.md, an Application exists once a Job clears dedup+match against a SearchProfile, starts before tailoring (TailoredApplication content is filled in once AI tailoring succeeds), and is reviewed/edited by the user before applying.

Grill: the full state list (e.g. pending_tailoring, needs_review, ready, applied, rejected, and whether states like "tailoring_failed" need to exist if regeneration exhausts retries), which transitions are user-triggered (dashboard actions) vs system-triggered (pipeline events), whether a user can manually edit tailored content and what that does to status, and whether closed/terminal states (applied, rejected, withdrawn) are ever reopened.
design:
## Application status-tracking flow (v1)

### States (single `status` enum column on Application)

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending_tailoring` | Created on Job dedup+match; also reused as the "regenerating" state (may still reference a prior valid TailoredApplication as fallback while a new attempt runs) |
| `tailoring_failed` | Regeneration retries exhausted; visible on dashboard with a manual retry action |
| `needs_review` | Current TailoredApplication is fact-valid; user can edit, regenerate, apply, or reject from here |
| `applied` | User manually marked it after submitting the application themselves on the platform (no auto-submit, no platform status polling) |
| `rejected` | User decided not to pursue this Job (covers both a pre-tailoring drop and a post-review drop; no separate `withdrawn` state) |

### Schema additions on Application

- `status` (enum, the 5 values above)
- `current_tailored_application_id` (nullable FK; retained across a regenerate until the new attempt replaces it, not cleared immediately)
- `applied_at` (nullable timestamp)
- `rejected_at` (nullable timestamp)
- `previous_status` (set only at the moment of a terminal transition into `applied`/`rejected`; powers Undo — no full status-history table)
- `edited_by_user` (nullable boolean, optional; editing tailored content does not itself change `status`)

### Transitions

| From | To | Trigger | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| (create) | `pending_tailoring` | system: Job clears dedup+match | |
| `pending_tailoring` | `needs_review` | system: tailoring succeeds fact validation | sends Telegram notification (the "come review this" moment) |
| `pending_tailoring` | `tailoring_failed` | system: regeneration retries exhausted | no per-Application Telegram ping — folds into n58.7's consecutive-failure alerting, not a separate channel |
| `pending_tailoring` | `rejected` | user: reject | `previous_status = pending_tailoring` |
| `tailoring_failed` | `pending_tailoring` | user: retry | |
| `tailoring_failed` | `rejected` | user: reject | `previous_status = tailoring_failed` |
| `needs_review` | `pending_tailoring` | user: regenerate | old TailoredApplication stays referenced/visible ("regenerating…") until replaced |
| `needs_review` | `applied` | user: mark applied | sets `applied_at` |
| `needs_review` | `rejected` | user: reject | `previous_status = needs_review`, sets `rejected_at` |
| `applied` | `needs_review` | user: undo | clears `applied_at` |
| `rejected` | `previous_status` | user: undo | clears `rejected_at`; restores exact prior status, not a fixed one |

### Non-status actions

- Editing tailored CV/cover-letter content in place: available while `needs_review`, does not change `status`.
- No reject-reason/notes field for v1 (no stated use case; easy to add later as a nullable column).

### UI shape

Named per-status action buttons (Reject / Retry / Regenerate / Mark Applied / Undo) driven off current `status` — not a free "change status to anything" dropdown. Avoids reachable-but-nonsensical states (e.g. jumping `pending_tailoring` straight to `applied` with no TailoredApplication to show).

### Out of scope for v1

- Tracking downstream real-world outcomes (employer-rejected, interview, offer) — would require authenticated platform integration, a different risk class than the read-only search APIs validated in n58.1.
- Status-change history log — per-state timestamps are enough; no stated need to reconstruct the full transition sequence.

Grilled and confirmed with user: 4 rounds, 15 questions total.
notes: Grilling round 1 in progress (8 questions on status modeling, pending-stage rejection, review/ready collapse, rejected/withdrawn semantics, applied semantics, tailoring-failure visibility, edit effect on status, terminal-state reopening).
close_reason: Application status flow grilled and confirmed with user (4 rounds, 15 questions). Full state list, transition table, schema fields, and undo/notification semantics recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md Application definition sharpened to match (single status enum, no separate ready state, rejected covers withdrawn, terminal undo).

title: Design MasterProfile schema and dashboard form
description:
## Question

What fields make up MasterProfile (the user's ground-truth work history, skills, education, projects — the source of truth TailoredApplication facts must match exactly), and how is it authored/edited via a dashboard form (confirmed: form-based, not a config file)?

Grill: structure of an experience entry (title, company, period, description/achievements — the fields TailoredApplication may not alter vs. may reframe), how skills and projects are represented (free text vs. structured/taggable), education entries, and what the dashboard form needs to support editing all of this (single-user, no-auth). Also confirm: is MasterProfile a single record, or versioned/snapshotted so a past TailoredApplication can be traced to the profile state it was generated from?
design:
## MasterProfile schema (v1)

Storage: single mutable `master_profiles` row (singleton, no user_id, not versioned) + relational
child tables (hasMany from MasterProfile): `experiences`, `educations`, `projects`. `skills` is a
JSON column on MasterProfile itself.

### MasterProfile (personal info)

 Field                 | Type                              | Notes
------------------------|------------------------------------|----------------------------------
 full_name             | string, required                  | fact
 email                 | string, required                  | fact
 phone                 | string, nullable                  | fact
 location              | string, nullable                  | fact
 professional_summary  | text, nullable                    | reframeable
 links                 | JSON {label, url}[]                | free-form, not fixed columns
 skills                | JSON {category: string, skills: string[]}[] | free-form user-defined categories

### Experience (hasMany, sorted by start_date desc)

title, company, location? (facts) | start_date, end_date?, is_current bool (facts, month+year
precision) | employment_type? enum (fact) | description text (reframeable) | achievements
string[] (reframeable) | skills_used? tags (fact, references skills)

### Education (hasMany, sorted by start_date desc)

institution, degree, field_of_study (facts) | start_date, end_date?, is_current bool (facts) |
description? text (reframeable - GPA/honors/coursework go here freeform, no dedicated fields)

### Project (hasMany, sorted by start_date desc, standalone - not linked to Experience)

name, start_date?, end_date?, is_current bool, tech_stack tags, link? url (facts) | description
text (reframeable) | achievements? string[] (reframeable)

## Decisions

- Single mutable record, no versioning/snapshotting. TailoredApplication's own copy of the facts
  it used (title/company/period etc, already required to match exactly) is sufficient audit
  trail; a full version-history table was rejected as unneeded complexity for a single-user tool
  edited infrequently.
- Fact/reframe split (locked architecturally for Experience) applies uniformly across Experience,
  Education, and Project: identifying/structural fields are immutable facts, only free-text
  `description`/`achievements` fields are AI-reframeable.
- MasterProfile's scope is sharpened beyond CONTEXT.md's original "work history, skills,
  education, and projects" to also include personal/contact info (name, email, phone, location,
  links, professional summary) - needed as the CV header's source of truth and naturally belongs
  with the rest of the ground-truth data.
- Links are a free-form {label, url}[] list, not fixed columns (linkedin_url etc) - avoids a
  migration every time a new link type appears.
- Skills are a categorized tag list (JSON column on MasterProfile, not a child table) - no
  per-skill fact/reframe distinction to track, so no need for row-level addressability.
- Experience/Education/Project are separate relational child tables (not JSON blobs on
  MasterProfile) - idiomatic Laravel, each entry independently addressable, maps directly to
  per-row CRUD on the dashboard form.
- No manual ordering - lists are always sorted by start_date descending (reverse-chronological,
  standard CV convention). No display_order field, no reorder UI.
- No per-entry inclusion/visibility toggle for v1 - every MasterProfile entry always feeds every
  TailoredApplication generation. Deferred as a `hidden` boolean addable later if it turns out to
  be needed; no stated use case yet.
- Dates are month+year precision only (day defaults to 1st internally, never shown/collected).
- `is_current` is an explicit boolean per Experience/Education entry (not inferred from null
  end_date), so "still ongoing" is unambiguous from "not filled in yet" in both DB and form UI;
  checking it disables/clears end_date.
- No completeness gating before triggering generation - single-user tool, profile will be filled
  in thoroughly before first use; not worth designing a "what counts as complete" rule.
- Dashboard form: one single scrollable page, all sections stacked (personal info -> skills ->
  experience -> education -> projects), singleton record auto-available (no explicit "create
  profile" step), per-row CRUD for each list.
- Form validates end_date >= start_date and blocks save on violation; end_date required unless
  is_current is checked.

Grilled and confirmed with user: 3 rounds, 16 questions total.
notes: Amended by applyr-n58.6 (CV template design): added photo_path (nullable) and show_photo (boolean) fields to MasterProfile personal info, to support an optional CV header photo. Schema table above is otherwise unchanged.
close_reason: MasterProfile schema grilled and confirmed with user (3 rounds, 16 questions). Full schema (personal info, Experience/Education/Project child tables, skills JSON, dashboard form design) recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md MasterProfile definition sharpened to include personal/contact info and the fact/reframe rule.

title: Design SearchProfile schema
description:
## Question

What fields make up a SearchProfile (the saved set of search parameters matched against job boards)? The user named keyword, lokasi (location), min pengalaman (minimum experience), and rentang tanggal post (post-date range) as the starting set — grill to confirm exact shape/types for each, whether a user can have multiple SearchProfiles active at once (implied yes, per the map's "one Application per Job regardless of how many SearchProfiles matched it" decision), how a SearchProfile maps onto each platform's own search/filter parameters (Glints and JobStreet may not expose identical filters), and any other fields needed (e.g. job type, remote/onsite, salary floor) that weren't in the original list.
design:
## SearchProfile schema (v1)

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| name | string, required | User-facing label; needed since multiple profiles can be active at once |
| is_active | boolean | Paused profiles skipped by poller, history retained |
| keyword | string[] | OR-matched terms |
| location | string | Free text (e.g. "Jakarta Selatan"); resolved to each platform's own location IDs at adapter level |
| country_code | string, unconstrained | Dynamic/no enum; only "ID" functionally supported until a non-Indonesia adapter variant exists (JobStreet is domain-per-country, not param-per-country) |
| min_experience_years | integer, nullable | |
| max_experience_years | integer, nullable | |
| post_date_range | enum: PAST_24_HOURS \| PAST_WEEK \| PAST_MONTH \| ANY_TIME | Matches Glints' actual bucketed capability, not an arbitrary date range |
| work_arrangement | enum: remote \| onsite \| hybrid \| any | |
| job_type | enum: full_time \| part_time \| contract \| internship \| any | |

## Decisions
- Multiple active SearchProfiles per user, run independently.
- Canonical schema + per-Adapter best-effort translation to native query params (see CONTEXT.md SearchProfile entry).
- Salary floor excluded from v1 (deferred as post-fetch display/sort concern, not a search filter).
- No operational/run-state fields on SearchProfile (last-run timestamp, dedup cursor belongs to n58.7's polling/scheduling design, not this schema).
- Reference facts pulled from applyr-n58.1 findings: Glints searchJobsV3 input fields (SearchTerm, CountryCode, HierarchicalLocationId*/CityId, lastUpdatedAtRange enum, min/maxYearsOfExperience, isRemote, workArrangementOptions); JobStreet jobSearchV7 exact keyword/location/date-range placement still unresolved (adapter-build mechanical follow-up, not a schema blocker).
close_reason: SearchProfile schema grilled and confirmed with user (9 questions, 2 rounds). Full field table recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md SearchProfile definition sharpened to match.

title: Investigate Glints & JobStreet internal JSON APIs
description:
## Question

Do Glints and JobStreet expose an internal JSON API (reachable without auth, without triggering anti-bot blocking) that a job-search Adapter could call directly, or does the Adapter need to fall back to HTML-selector parsing / Browsershot headless browsing for one or both platforms?

Investigate Glints first, then JobStreet, in the same session. For each platform: search a role with typical params (keyword, location, date range) in a real browser, inspect network requests for JSON XHR/fetch calls that return job listing data, and try calling that endpoint directly (no browser) to see if it responds normally or gets blocked/challenged. Note any auth/session/cookie requirements, rate-limit signals, and response shape (what fields are present).

This is a high-risk prototype ticket per the map's Destination: it validates external facts (not a design preference) that the Job canonical-model ticket and the monitoring/alerting ticket both depend on.
notes:
## Findings

### Glints — API confirmed usable directly, no fallback needed

- Search page (`glints.com/id/opportunities/jobs/explore`) is a Next.js app, loads fine unauthenticated, SSRs initial results into an Apollo-cache blob (`__NEXT_DATA__`).
- GraphQL endpoint: `POST https://glints.com/api/v2/graphql` (candidate-facing client; `/api/graphql` and `/api/v2-alc/graphql` also exist for other client variants).
- No auth needed — response body includes `"isAuthenticated": false` when called with zero cookies.
- Anti-bot: Cloudflare fronts it. A generic bare `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0` gets hard-blocked (`403`, `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`, Cloudflare "Firewall" interstitial). A realistic full desktop Chrome UA string alone — no cookies, no Referer — was enough to pass. Bot-scoring here appears to key mainly off UA plausibility, not a JS/Turnstile challenge.
- No rate-limiting observed across 15 rapid sequential requests.
- Schema introspection is **enabled** in production — queried the live schema directly.
- Confirmed working query: `searchJobsV3(data: JobSearchConditionInput): JobSearchResults`.
  - Relevant input fields: `SearchTerm` (keyword list), `CountryCode`, `HierarchicalLocationIdLevel1-4`/`CityId` (location), `lastUpdatedAtRange` (enum: `PAST_24_HOURS`/`PAST_WEEK`/`PAST_MONTH`/`ANY_TIME` — **bucketed, not an arbitrary date range**), `minYearsOfExperience`/`maxYearsOfExperience`, `isRemote`, `workArrangementOptions`, `page`/`pageSize`/`offset`/`limit`, `sortBy`, `sources`.
  - Result shape: `totalJobs`, `hasMore`, `jobsInPage: [Job]`.
  - `Job` fields available: id, title, company{id,name}, city/citySubDivision/country/location, createdAt/updatedAt/startDate/endDate/expiryDate, min/maxYearsOfExperience, isRemote, workArrangementOption, salaries/salaryEstimate, skills, benefits, descriptionJsonString, externalApplyURL, status, type, source, educationLevel, gender, labels.
  - Ran a live end-to-end query for "software engineer" / Indonesia / PAST_WEEK and got real current postings back.
- **Verdict: use the JSON API directly. No HTML-selector parsing or Browsershot needed for Glints job search.**

### JobStreet — API confirmed reachable, exact request shape not fully pinned down

- Domain: `jobstreet.co.id` now 308-redirects to `id.jobstreet.com` (SEEK's consolidated domain, same backend platform as SEEK AU/NZ and JobsDB). **Adapter should target `id.jobstreet.com`.**
- GraphQL endpoint: same-origin proxy at `https://id.jobstreet.com/graphql` (backs onto `candidate-graphql(-dark)-prod.cloud.seek.com.au`).
- Anti-bot: Cloudflare fronts it, and it's more header-sensitive than Glints — a request missing standard browser headers (`Accept`, `Accept-Language`, `sec-ch-ua*`) on the plain HTML search page itself gets hard-blocked (`403`, `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`, Turnstile CSP present). Adding a full realistic header set (proper `Accept`/`Accept-Language`/`sec-ch-ua*` plus a real UA) got a normal `200` with real SSR job data embedded (`totalCount` present) — no JS challenge actually had to be solved in this test.
- With that same header set, POSTing directly to `/graphql` (no cookies, no auth) reaches the real Apollo Server and returns real GraphQL validation errors, not a block. No blocking/rate-limiting observed across 10 rapid identical requests.
- Introspection is **disabled** in production (Apollo Server hardening) — had to recover the schema from the frontend's minified JS bundles instead.
- Found the real operation used by the search results page: `jobSearchV7(params: JobSearchV7QueryInput!)`, called alongside `$locale`/`$zone`/`$country`/`$timezone`/`$tagsSubType`. Extracted the full ~300-line field selection the live frontend actually requests, which includes: id, title, abstract, advertiser/organisation, categories, location (incl. seoHierarchy), work types/work arrangements, salary (min/max/currency/period + display value), listedAt (posted date), tags, url, and activity/analytics counts (impressions, application starts/ends) — richer than Glints in some respects (salary display formatting, activity stats).
  - Live validation-error probing (GraphQL errors are precise about missing/unknown fields) confirmed `params` requires only `searchContext: JobSearchV7SearchContextInput!` and `sessionId: String!` at the top level; `searchContext` in turn requires `brand`/`intent`/`source` enums (plausible values recovered from the bundle: brand `"jobstreet"`, intent `"SEARCH"`, source `"FE_REVERSAL"`; not yet confirmed which combination is canonical for a fresh keyword search).
  - **Open item**: exactly where keyword / location / date-range / pagination land in the input shape wasn't resolved this session — they're not direct children of `params` or `searchContext` as tried. The frontend maps URL query params into these GraphQL variables via a client-side step this investigation didn't fully trace. This is a mechanical follow-up (e.g. capture one real outgoing request from an actual browser devtools session) for whoever builds the JobStreet adapter — not a feasibility blocker.
  - `sessionId` is a client-generated value (from Redux state), not a server-issued auth/session cookie — a request-shape requirement, not an auth requirement.
- **Verdict: the JSON API is real and reachable directly, unauthenticated, without anti-bot blocking, given realistic browser headers.** Finishing the exact `JobSearchV7QueryInput` shape is adapter-implementation detail, not a reason to fall back to HTML/Browsershot.

### Answer to the ticket's question

Neither platform needs to fall back to HTML-selector parsing or Browsershot headless browsing for job search. Both expose internal GraphQL JSON APIs reachable directly over plain HTTP, unauthenticated, provided requests carry realistic browser-like headers (User-Agent alone sufficed for Glints; a fuller standard header set was needed for JobStreet). Cloudflare fronts both, but in this session its bot-scoring was satisfied by header realism alone — no JS challenge had to be solved, no login/cookies/session required. No rate-limiting surfaced in short bursts (10-15 rapid sequential requests) on either platform; that doesn't rule out slower-forming, volume-based throttling, so the real adapter should still pace requests and back off on 403/429 — and the monitoring/alerting ticket (n58.7) should treat a Cloudflare challenge response (`403` + `Cf-Mitigated: challenge` header) as the concrete signal to alert on.

### Notes for downstream tickets

- **Job canonical model (n58.5)**: use the union of Glints' `Job` fields and JobStreet's `JobSearchV7` job fields above as the field-shape reference.
- **Adapter monitoring/alerting (n58.7)**: alert on Cloudflare challenge responses (`403` + `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`) — that's the observed anti-bot escalation signature for both platforms.
- **JobStreet domain**: target `id.jobstreet.com`, not `jobstreet.co.id` (which redirects).

No fallback to HTML-selector parsing or Browsershot needed for job search on either platform. Cloudflare bot-mitigation on both was satisfied by realistic browser headers alone in this session; JobStreet's exact query-variable shape needs a small mechanical follow-up when the adapter is actually built.
